method: Five sequential arms, three fresh NEAR-only wallets each. Router-only startup control, parallel four-role startup, the same candidate with apac-ne placement, repeated parallel-startup control, repeated Router-only control. SDK, Gateway and harness stay fixed. Placement uses fresh wallet objects; all original versions are restored.

failure.boundary: First-sign NEAR implicit-account funding after Yao registration completed
failure.timingCoverage: No completed browser timing sample for the failed wallet; role telemetry includes all three control-after Yao executions.

decisions: Keep parallel startup. It started the exact Router, A, B and Signing Worker objects before required work in all measured parallel arms.
Keep broad apac placement. The apac-ne candidate was slower than both broad-apac parallel-startup arms.
Do not claim a stable 2.45-second setup result. The version-matched repeated parallel arm measured 3.852 seconds median.
Moving coordination into the Router object could remove the roughly 50 ms finish dispatch, but the initial dispatch remains. Larger placement gains are unmeasured.
Signing Worker delivery has substantial time outside the object handler. First-work object CPU was 24 and 29 ms median in the two broad-apac parallel arms; delivery callers measured 137 and 587 ms.
limits: Provider CPU and wall times describe whole invocations, not individual cryptographic operations.
Application clocks freeze during CPU work; application spans are not transport timers.
Small sequential samples do not establish a latency percentile or placement success rate.
D1 counts cover bound-root loads only; total Gateway D1 and backend Console calls are unavailable.
No diagnostic location fetches were added. Physical colocation is not proved.
Per-operation CPU profiles and internal payload-byte counts are unavailable.
The final control has two complete browser samples and three Yao server traces. One first-sign funding RPC returned 408 after Yao completed.
First work per role is the first non-startup command observed for a fresh wallet. That boundary is preparation for A/B and delivery for Signing Worker.
Nested and overlapping application intervals cannot be added or subtracted from independent provider clocks to derive exact network time.
The 1–2 second median hosted Yao target remains unmet.

Deployment API versions do not prove which version served an invocation. Eligible latency statistics exclude any wallet with a mismatched custody version during startup or setup; raw arm summaries are retained.
